questions.question: On 16 July 2025, India achieved a major milestone by successfully destroying two aerial high-speed unmanned targets at high altitude in Ladakh using the upgraded variant of the Akash Weapon System for the Indian Army called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akash Prime**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **16 July 2025**, India successfully destroyed two high-speed unmanned aerial targets at high altitude in the Ladakh region, marking a significant milestone in the country's defense capabilities.
 
• This achievement was accomplished using the **Akash Prime**, the upgraded variant of the Akash Weapon System designed specifically for the **Indian Army**.
 
• The **Akash Prime** is an advanced surface-to-air missile system that incorporates several improvements over its predecessor, including enhanced guidance systems, better accuracy, and the ability to operate in extreme weather conditions.
 
• The test conducted in Ladakh demonstrated the **system's capability to neutralize aerial threats at high altitudes**, making it particularly suitable for defending India's borders in mountainous regions.
 
• The Akash Weapon System, including its **Prime variant**, is part of India’s push toward achieving self-reliance in defense technology under the **‘Make in India’ initiative.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akash Prime:**

 
 
• The **Akash Prime** is an upgraded version of the Akash surface-to-air missile system developed by the **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• It is equipped with an **indigenously developed active RF seeker** for improved target tracking and interception.
 
• The system is capable of engaging multiple targets simultaneously and can operate in a variety of challenging environments.
 
• The Akash Prime can target **enemy aircraft, drones, and cruise missiles**, providing a robust layer of defense.
 
 
 
• **BrahMos:**
 
 
• The **BrahMos** is a supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia.
 
• It is known for its high speed, precision, and ability to be launched from land, sea, and air platforms.
 
• Unlike Akash Prime, BrahMos is primarily an offensive missile designed for precision strikes on ground and naval targets.
 
 
 
• **Pinaka:**
 
 
• **Pinaka** is a multi-barrel rocket launcher system developed by DRDO and is used by the Indian Army.
 
• It is designed for area saturation and is capable of launching a salvo of rockets in a short period to neutralize enemy positions.
 
• Pinaka is not a surface-to-air missile system and thus is not relevant to countering aerial threats.
 
 
 
• **Other Akash Variants:**
 
 
• The original **Akash Weapon System** was developed as a medium-range surface-to-air missile system for the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• It has been deployed by both the **Indian Army and Air Force** to provide air defense against enemy aircraft and missiles.
 
• The **Akash Advanced** is another variant focused on enhanced range and lethality, but it lacks some of the specific advancements found in Akash Prime.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Test:**
 
 
• The successful test of Akash Prime in Ladakh underscores India’s capability to defend its high-altitude borders effectively.
 
• It reflects the growing indigenization of defense technology under the **‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ initiative**.
 
• With advanced systems like Akash Prime, India strengthens its preparedness against aerial threats in high-altitude regions like **Ladakh**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DRDO’s Role:**

 
 
• The **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** is the primary agency behind the design and development of the Akash Weapon System and its variants.
 
• DRDO is a key player in India’s defense self-reliance initiatives, producing a range of weapon systems and technologies.
 
 
 
• **High-Altitude Defense:**
 
 
• High-altitude regions like Ladakh pose unique challenges for defense systems due to thin air, extreme temperatures, and rugged terrain.
 
• The Akash Prime’s successful test in this environment demonstrates its suitability for deployment in such areas.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• The Akash Prime is a product of India’s **‘Make in India’ initiative**, which aims to reduce dependence on foreign defense imports.
 
• It also highlights India’s capability to develop advanced technologies indigenously.

questions.question: Where was the first-ever International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Assembly held in India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first-ever International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Assembly** was held in **New Delhi**, India, in **June 2025**.
 
• The IBCA was established to protect and conserve **big cats** such as lions, tigers, leopards, cheetahs, jaguars, and snow leopards, which are facing threats due to habitat loss, poaching, and human-wildlife conflict.
 
• The assembly focused on building global cooperation to ensure the long-term conservation and survival of these majestic species.
 
• **New Delhi**, being the capital city of India, was chosen as the venue to emphasize India's commitment to wildlife conservation and its leadership role in the global conservation community.
 
• The event saw participation from member countries, conservation organizations, researchers, and policymakers aiming to strengthen partnerships and share best practices for big cat conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA):**

 
 
• The IBCA was launched as a global initiative by India to protect big cats, with a focus on **cooperative conservation efforts**.
 
• It aims to bring together countries and organizations working on big cat conservation under a unified platform to share knowledge, resources, and strategies.
 
• India has a rich legacy of big cat conservation, including iconic species like the Bengal tiger, Asiatic lion, and leopard.
 
 
 
• **Big Cats and Their Global Importance:**
 
 
• Big cats are apex predators and play a crucial role in maintaining the balance of ecosystems.
 
• Species like tigers, lions, and cheetahs are considered keystone species, meaning their presence ensures the health and stability of their habitats.
 
• Conservation of big cats also has a cultural and economic significance, as they attract ecotourism and are symbols of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **India's Role in Big Cat Conservation:**
 
 
• India is home to several big cat species, including the **Bengal tiger**, **Asiatic lion**, and **leopard**.
 
• India has successfully implemented conservation programs such as **Project Tiger** (launched in 1973) and **Project Lion** to protect and increase the population of these species.
 
• India also reintroduced cheetahs in 2022 under the **Cheetah Reintroduction Project**, making it a global leader in wildlife conservation.
 
 
 
• **Global Threats to Big Cats:**
 
 
• Big cats face threats such as habitat loss due to deforestation, human encroachment, and urbanization.
 
• Illegal wildlife trade and poaching remain significant challenges, fueled by demand for big cat skins, bones, and other parts.
 
• Human-wildlife conflict is another major issue, particularly in areas where big cats and humans share close proximity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Conservation Efforts:**

 
 
• Organizations like the **World Wildlife Fund (WWF)** and the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** are actively involved in big cat conservation.
 
• Programs such as the **Global Tiger Initiative** and **Snow Leopard Trust** aim to conserve specific big cat species and their habitats.
 
 
 
• **India’s Conservation Milestones:**
 
 
• India hosts over **70% of the world’s tiger population** and has successfully increased their numbers through dedicated conservation efforts.
 
• The **Gir Forest National Park** in Gujarat is the last refuge of the Asiatic lion, and conservation efforts have helped stabilize their population.

questions.question: What was India’s overall score in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for the year 2024 released in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**38**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's overall score in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for 2024** was **38**, as released in February 2025.
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** is an annual report published by **Transparency International** which ranks countries based on perceived levels of public sector corruption.
 
• The score of **38** indicates that India has a moderate corruption level, as the CPI scoring system ranges from **0 (highly corrupt)** to **100 (very clean)**.
 
• India's ranking in the CPI is influenced by factors such as **governance, transparency, and institutional integrity**.
 
• This score is consistent with India's ongoing efforts to combat corruption through measures like **Digital India initiatives, e-governance, and improved judicial mechanisms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):**

 
 
• The CPI is a globally recognized index published by **Transparency International**, a non-governmental organization headquartered in Berlin, Germany.
 
• It ranks countries based on perceptions of corruption in the **public sector**, using data from multiple surveys and expert assessments.
 
• A score of **0** represents a highly corrupt nation, while a score of **100** indicates a corruption-free nation.
 
• The index covers **180 countries** and territories worldwide.
 
 
 
• **India’s Performance in Recent Years:**
 
 
• India's CPI score has fluctuated between **36 and 40** in the last decade, reflecting challenges in governance and anti-corruption measures.
 
• In the CPI for 2023 (released in 2024), India's score was **36**, indicating a slight improvement in the 2024 score of **38**.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in CPI:**
 
 
• Countries like **Denmark, Finland, and New Zealand** consistently rank at the top of the CPI with scores above **85**, reflecting low levels of corruption.
 
• Countries with the lowest scores include **Somalia, Syria, and South Sudan**, with scores below **15**, indicating severe corruption challenges.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Curb Corruption in India:**
 
 
• Implementation of the **Right to Information (RTI) Act** to enhance transparency and accountability in governance.
 
• Introduction of **e-Governance** initiatives like **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to reduce leakages in welfare schemes.
 
• Efforts to strengthen anti-corruption agencies like the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)** and the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Methodology of CPI:**

 
 
• The CPI aggregates data from **13 different sources**, including surveys conducted by organizations like the **World Bank** and the **World Economic Forum**.
 
• These sources assess corruption in areas like **bribery, misuse of public funds, and nepotism**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Anti-Corruption Success:**
 
 
• Countries like **Estonia** and **Georgia** have significantly improved their CPI scores by implementing **e-governance and judicial reforms**.
 
• India's initiatives like **GST implementation** and the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC)** have contributed to improving transparency.

questions.question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, published in June 2025, India’s installed renewable energy capacity rose from 64.04 watts per capita in 2014–15 to 156.31 watts per capita in 2024–25. This growth primarily supports which Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SDG 7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 is focused on ensuring **access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all**. The growth in renewable energy capacity directly supports this goal.
 
• As per the **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025**, India's installed renewable energy capacity increased from **64.04 watts per capita in 2014–15 to 156.31 watts per capita in 2024–25**, showcasing significant progress in renewable energy development.
 
• This increase aligns with SDG 7, specifically targeting the **expansion of renewable energy** to ensure sustainability and reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• The promotion of renewable energy also contributes to reducing **greenhouse gas emissions**, indirectly supporting other SDGs like SDG 13 (Climate Action).
 
• India’s renewable energy initiatives, including solar, wind, and hydroelectric power projects, play a key role in achieving the targets set under SDG 7 by ensuring sustainable energy production and consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 7:**

 
 
• SDG 7 aims to ensure universal access to **modern energy services**, improve energy efficiency, and increase the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix.
 
• It is one of the 17 SDGs adopted by the **United Nations** in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
 
• Key targets under SDG 7 include achieving universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services by **2030**, and substantially increasing the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has set a target of achieving **500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity** by 2030 under its updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
 
• The country has launched several initiatives, such as the **National Solar Mission**, to promote solar energy and achieve **net-zero emissions** by 2070.
 
• India is also a founding member of the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**, which promotes the use of solar energy worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Renewable Energy on Other SDGs:**
 
 
• While SDG 7 specifically focuses on energy, renewable energy development also contributes to other goals like SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
 
• For instance, reducing reliance on fossil fuels helps mitigate climate change, directly supporting SDG 13.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• SDG 13 (Climate Action): While renewable energy supports climate action by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, it is not the primary SDG linked to the renewable energy capacity metric mentioned in the question.
 
• SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure): This goal emphasizes innovation and infrastructure development. While renewable energy infrastructure contributes to this SDG, it is not the primary focus.
 
• SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production): This goal focuses on sustainable consumption and production patterns but is not directly linked to the renewable energy capacity metric.

questions.question: From 1 May 2025, which of the following portals did the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandate stakeholders to use?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PRAVAAH Portal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has mandated stakeholders to use the **PRAVAAH Portal** from **1 May 2025**.
 
• **PRAVAAH** stands for **Platform for Regulatory Application, Validation, and Authorization**, developed by the **RBI** to streamline regulatory processes and interactions between regulated entities and the central bank.
 
• The portal aims to provide a **digital mechanism for regulatory applications**, reducing paperwork and enhancing processing efficiency.
 
• It is part of the **RBI's digital transformation initiatives** to improve transparency and accountability in regulatory processes.
 
• The platform will be utilized for submitting, tracking, and managing regulatory applications and approvals by banks, NBFCs, and other regulated entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SAKSHAM Portal:**

 
 
• **SAKSHAM** stands for **System for Authority and Knowledge Sharing for Holistic Access to Management.**
 
• This portal is used by various ministries and departments for tracking and monitoring the implementation of government schemes and initiatives.
 
• It is primarily focused on enhancing the efficiency of governance-related processes.
 
 
 
• **SEVA Portal:**
 
 
• The **SEVA Portal** is an initiative of the **Ministry of Power** to address consumer grievances related to electricity services.
 
• It provides a platform to raise complaints and track their resolution by state electricity boards and DISCOMs.
 
• It is not related to the regulatory framework of the RBI.
 
 
 
• **VITARAN Portal:**
 
 
• **VITARAN** is an online platform developed for **electricity distribution companies** to manage billing, payments, and consumer information.
 
• It is aimed at improving operational efficiency in the energy sector and enhancing consumer satisfaction.
 
• This portal is unrelated to the RBI's regulatory functions.
 
 
 
• **PRAVAAH Portal Features:**
 
 
• The portal will provide a **centralized mechanism for submitting and processing applications** like licensing, renewals, and other regulatory approvals.
 
• Stakeholders will benefit from **real-time tracking of application status** and notifications for updates.
 
• The platform is expected to reduce delays and improve the overall efficiency of regulatory processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Reforms by RBI:**

 
 
• The RBI has been undertaking various reforms to digitize and streamline regulatory mechanisms in India.
 
• Platforms like **PRAVAAH** are aligned with the objective of enhancing the ease of doing business and improving compliance processes for regulated entities.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Timeline:**
 
 
• The mandatory use of the PRAVAAH portal will begin from **1 May 2025**, giving stakeholders sufficient time to adapt to the new system.
 
• This timeline reflects the RBI's efforts to ensure a smooth transition for all stakeholders involved.

questions.question: In May 2025, which state/union territory government approved five cloud-seeding trials at an outlay of ₹3.21 crore to combat air pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi government** approved five cloud-seeding trials in **May 2025** to combat the severe issue of **air pollution**, specifically smog and particulate matter.
 
• An amount of **₹3.21 crore** was allocated for these trials, showcasing a significant step toward implementing scientific methods to tackle environmental issues.
 
• **Cloud seeding** is a weather modification technique that involves dispersing substances like **silver iodide** or **potassium iodide** into the atmosphere to induce rainfall. This helps in reducing airborne pollutants by bringing them to the ground.
 
• The initiative was taken in response to worsening air quality in Delhi, which has consistently ranked as one of the most polluted cities globally according to the **World Air Quality Index**.
 
• This effort aligns with the broader environmental goals of the **National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi** to improve public health and mitigate the adverse impacts of pollution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **What is Cloud Seeding?**

 
 
• Cloud seeding is a form of **weather modification** where chemicals like **silver iodide**, **potassium iodide**, or dry ice are dispersed into clouds to encourage precipitation.
 
• The method is used globally for purposes like **rain enhancement**, **snowpack augmentation**, and **hail suppression**.
 
• It helps in **reducing air pollution** by washing down particulate matter and other pollutants from the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Air Pollution in Delhi:**
 
 
• Delhi faces severe air pollution due to factors like **vehicular emissions**, **industrial activities**, **construction dust**, and **stubble burning** in nearby states.
 
• During winter, the pollution levels worsen due to the formation of **smog**, which is a mixture of smoke and fog.
 
• The **Air Quality Index (AQI)** often crosses hazardous levels, causing respiratory and cardiovascular health issues.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Measures Taken by the Delhi Government:**
 
 
• Implementation of the **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** to tackle pollution during high-risk periods.
 
• Promotion of **electric vehicles (EVs)** under the **Delhi EV Policy**.
 
• Introduction of the **Odd-Even Traffic Scheme** to reduce vehicular emissions.
 
• Deployment of air purifiers and **anti-smog guns** at construction sites.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of Cloud Seeding:**
 
 
• The **United Arab Emirates** uses cloud seeding to enhance rainfall in its arid climate.
 
• **China** deployed extensive cloud seeding programs during the **2008 Beijing Olympics** to ensure clear skies.
 
• The **United States** uses cloud seeding in states like **Colorado** and **Wyoming** to increase snowpack for water resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Effectiveness of Cloud Seeding:** While cloud seeding is a promising solution, its effectiveness depends on the availability of suitable clouds and specific atmospheric conditions.
 
• **Health Impacts of Air Pollution:** Long-term exposure to pollutants like PM2.5 and PM10 can lead to **respiratory diseases**, **cardiovascular problems**, and reduced life expectancy.
 
• **International Support:** Many countries, including **Germany** and **Japan**, are collaborating with India to share expertise and technology for pollution control.
 
• **Public Awareness Campaigns:** The Delhi government also conducts campaigns to educate the public about pollution control measures and the importance of sustainable practices.

questions.question: What is the full form of RIMES, an intergovernmental body in news in 2025?

options.text: Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System
Regional Institute for Meteorological and Environmental Studies
Risk Information and Monitoring of Emergency Situations
Research Initiative for Mitigating Environmental Shocks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System** (RIMES) is an intergovernmental institution designed to enhance regional capacities in disaster preparedness and mitigation.
 
• RIMES was established in collaboration with the **United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP)** in **2009** after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami.
 
• The organization provides **early warning systems** for natural hazards such as tsunamis, cyclones, floods, and droughts, thereby reducing the risks associated with these disasters.
 
• RIMES comprises **member states** from Asia, Africa, and the Pacific, including countries like India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, and others that are highly vulnerable to natural calamities.
 
• It works through collaborative efforts, offering **training, technical support, and forecasting tools** to member countries to strengthen their disaster management frameworks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background:**

 
 
• The establishment of RIMES was necessitated by the **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami**, which highlighted the lack of coordinated early warning systems in the region.
 
• RIMES was formally launched in **2009**, with its headquarters located in **Bangkok, Thailand**.
 
 
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• RIMES specializes in the **development of early warning systems** for multi-hazard scenarios, including weather-related and geophysical threats.
 
• It offers **technical assistance** to member countries in interpreting and applying hazard forecasts to mitigate risks.
 
• The organization also promotes **capacity building** by providing training programs for disaster risk reduction.
 
 
 
• **Member Countries:**
 
 
• RIMES has a membership of **22 countries**, including **India, Myanmar, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh**. Its services extend to over 40 countries worldwide.
 
• India is an active member and plays a significant role in disaster management initiatives under RIMES.
 
 
 
• **Technology and Tools:**
 
 
• RIMES utilizes advanced technologies such as **satellite imagery, climate modeling, and real-time monitoring** to provide accurate hazard predictions.
 
• It operates the **, which is equipped to monitor hazard events and disseminate alerts.
 
 
 
• Impact:**
 
 
• RIMES has significantly improved disaster preparedness in member states, enabling them to respond effectively to natural hazards.
 
• Its efforts have reduced the loss of lives and property, particularly in disaster-prone regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System__ – This is the correct answer as it accurately represents the full form and purpose of RIMES.
 
• **Option 2:** Regional Institute for Meteorological and Environmental Studies – This option is incorrect as it does not align with the objectives or structure of RIMES.
 
• **Option 3:** Risk Information and Monitoring of Emergency Situations – This is incorrect; RIMES focuses on early warning systems rather than emergency monitoring.
 
• **Option 4:** Research Initiative for Mitigating Environmental Shocks – This option is not valid as RIMES is primarily a disaster preparedness organization, not a research initiative.
 
• **Option 5:** Blank – This option is irrelevant as it does not provide any information.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• RIMES plays a vital role in disaster risk reduction, helping member countries build resilience against natural hazards.
 
• Its collaborative approach fosters international cooperation and the sharing of resources and expertise.

questions.question: Where was the first-ever national conference of Urban Local Body Chairpersons across Indian States and UTs inaugurated by the Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gurugram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first-ever national conference of **Urban Local Body Chairpersons** across Indian States and Union Territories was inaugurated by **Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla** in **July 2025**.
 
• The conference was held in **Gurugram, Haryana**, emphasizing the importance of urban governance and decentralized administration.
 
• The aim of the conference was to provide a platform for **Urban Local Body (ULB) leaders** to share ideas, experiences, and best practices for improving urban management.
 
• The event highlighted the role of ULBs in implementing **flagship government schemes** and addressing challenges such as urbanization, infrastructure development, waste management, and public services.
 
• Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla stressed the need for **strengthening local governance** and ensuring active participation of citizens in urban decision-making processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs):**

 
 
• ULBs are local government institutions responsible for managing urban areas such as cities and towns.
 
• They include municipal corporations, municipal councils, and town panchayats.
 
• ULBs play a key role in implementing policies related to **urban infrastructure**, sanitation, housing, transport, and public health.
 
• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act provides the framework for the functioning of Urban Local Bodies in India.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Decentralized Governance:**
 
 
• Decentralized governance ensures **efficient delivery** of services and empowers local communities to actively participate in decision-making.
 
• It promotes accountability and transparency in the administration of urban areas.
 
• Decentralization strengthens the role of local leaders in addressing specific urban challenges such as **traffic congestion** and waste management.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in India:**
 
 
• India is experiencing rapid urbanization, with **more than 34% of the population** living in urban areas as of 2021.
 
• Urbanization presents challenges such as **housing shortages**, pollution, and increased demand for basic services.
 
• Government schemes like **Smart Cities Mission** aim to address these challenges by modernizing urban infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Flagship Government Programs:**
 
 
• Programs such as **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)**, and **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** aim to improve urban living conditions.
 
• ULBs play a pivotal role in implementing these initiatives and ensuring their success.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Lok Sabha Speaker:**

 
 
• Shri Om Birla, as the Speaker of Lok Sabha, has been actively involved in initiatives to strengthen democratic institutions and governance at all levels.
 
• His participation in the conference underscores the importance of local governance in India's democratic framework.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Gurugram:**
 
 
• Gurugram is one of India's leading urban centers, known for its rapid development and modern infrastructure.
 
• The city serves as a hub for discussions on urban challenges and solutions, making it a fitting location for the conference.

questions.question: As per the June 2025 India Child Protection report, what percentage of 44,902 rescued children were found in the worst forms of child labour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.9%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **June 2025 India Child Protection report** highlighted the alarming situation of child labour in India.
 
• A total of **44,902 children** were rescued during the reporting period under child protection initiatives.
 
• Out of these rescued children, **0.9% were found in the worst forms of child labour**, which include hazardous industries, bonded labour, and child trafficking for labour exploitation.
 
• The term "worst forms of child labour" is defined under the **International Labour Organization (ILO) Convention No. 182**, which India ratified in **2017**. It includes activities that are hazardous or exploitative for children.
 
• The correct percentage is **0.9%**, which signifies the proportion of children engaged in these severe forms of exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Child Labour:**

 
 
• The term "child labour" refers to the employment of children in any work that deprives them of their childhood, interferes with their ability to attend school, and is mentally, physically, socially, or morally harmful.
 
• It is defined in the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986** in India.
 
 
 
• **Worst Forms of Child Labour:**
 
 
• Activities categorized under "worst forms" include **slavery or practices similar to slavery**, such as debt bondage, forced labour, and trafficking.
 
• Engagement in hazardous industries like mining, construction, and chemical production also falls under this category.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework in India:**
 
 
• The **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016** prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in any form of labour and adolescents (14-18 years) in hazardous occupations.
 
• The **Right to Education Act, 2009** ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years, addressing one of the root causes of child labour.
 
 
 
• **International Efforts:**
 
 
• The **ILO's International Programme on the Elimination of Child Labour (IPEC)** aims to eliminate child labour globally.
 
• India ratified the **ILO Convention No. 138** (Minimum Age Convention) and **No. 182** (Worst Forms of Child Labour Convention) in 2017, committing to abolishing child labour.
 
 
 
• **Important Statistics:**
 
 
• According to the **2021 UNICEF report**, approximately **160 million children** globally are engaged in child labour, with a significant proportion in hazardous work.
 
• In India, the **Census 2011** reported over **10 million children** engaged in child labour, though recent initiatives have significantly reduced this number.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives in India:**

 
 
• The **National Child Labour Project (NCLP)** scheme rehabilitates children withdrawn from child labour and provides them with education and vocational training.
 
• The **PENCIL portal** (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) was launched in 2017 to ensure effective enforcement of child labour laws.
 
 
 
• **Role of NGOs:**
 
 
• Organizations like **Bachpan Bachao Andolan** and **Child Rights and You (CRY)** have been instrumental in rescuing children and spreading awareness about child labour.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Eradicating Child Labour:**
 
 
• Poverty, lack of education, and social norms continue to drive child labour in India and globally.
 
• Effective enforcement of laws and rehabilitation of rescued children remain significant challenges.

questions.question: Which of the following insurance companies announced the adoption of the revised GST structure on all insurance products from 22 September 2025?

__
 
• **HDFC Life Insurance Co. Ltd.** announced the adoption of the **revised GST structure** on all its insurance products starting from **22 September 2025**.
 
• The implementation aligns with the Government of India’s initiative to ensure uniform taxation under the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** framework.
 
• This move is expected to bring transparency in pricing, enhance customer trust, and ensure compliance with the revised tax norms.

__
 
• **GST and Its Impact on Insurance:**

 
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is a comprehensive indirect tax introduced in India on **1 July 2017**.
 
• Under GST, insurance premiums are taxed at a standard rate, making tax compliance uniform across the industry.
 
• This taxation reform has simplified the previously complex structure of service tax and other indirect taxes applicable to insurance products.
 
 
 
• **About HDFC Life Insurance Co. Ltd.:**

• **Other Leading Insurance Companies:**

• **ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Co. Ltd.:** Offers customer-centric solutions and is one of the largest private life insurers in India.
 
• **Sahara India Life Insurance Co. Ltd.:** Was the first wholly Indian-owned private life insurance company in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Revised GST Structure:**
 
 
• Ensures uniform tax application across all insurance products.
 
• Eliminates cascading effects of taxation, bringing clarity and efficiency to the insurance sector.
 
• Provides better understanding and transparency to customers regarding the pricing of insurance policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Insurance Companies in GST Adoption:**

 
 
• Insurance companies, as financial institutions, play a key role in implementing GST by integrating tax reforms into their product pricing and operations.
 
• They are required to comply with periodic tax filings and ensure that tax benefits, if any, are passed on to customers.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries with GST systems, such as Australia and Canada, have seen significant improvements in tax compliance and simplification of indirect taxes.
 
• India’s adoption of GST in the insurance sector is part of a larger effort to align its tax policies with global standards.
